rv.q: It was put across, sometimes sensationally, by a supremely versatile cast.
If you love Porgy, treat yourself to this not-so-frequent opportunity to revel in its glories.

In the role of Porgy was bass-baritone Alfred Walker, who brought remarkable depth in his undertaking. Having had the chance to see Walker in the opposing role of Crown last time around, his performance was a captivating reminder of how versatile an artist can be.
In his Met conducting debut, Kwamé Ryan led a perfectly paced performance that crackled with energy and churned with emotion.
This was, truly, going out at the top.
